files: {dir}/{part}.mid with part in chords, arp, bass, lead, all
slide: note overlaps the next note by 60 ticks (1/32) at 480 ppq
s1_note: How the S-1 maps velocity/overlap to its own accent and slide is not verified.

confidence.constructed: concrete notes built from a rule the source states

synthwave.name: Synthwave / Darksynth
synthwave.why: ~100 BPM (outrun ~105, darksynth ~114); minor keys, Phrygian/Mixolydian, harmonic-minor V in darkwave.

acid.name: Acid house / techno
acid.why: Acid techno 130-140, Chicago acid 118-125; a pedal on one root, Dorian/Phrygian fragments.
acid.j6: Set 58 (Techno), set 57 (House/Techno, has C5b9 root+b9 stab)

deephouse.name: Deep house
deephouse.why: 118-124 BPM, minor keys, Dorian im7-IV7 vamps, m7/m9 voicings.

chicago.name: Chicago house
chicago.why: 118-125 BPM four-on-the-floor; offbeat stabs mirroring the open hat.

lofi.name: Lo-fi hip hop
lofi.why: 70-90 BPM (mostly 80-85), maj7/m7/9 chords held a bar or more; swing it on the OP-XY.
lofi.j6: Sets 68-69 (Lofi R&B), 72-81 (Neo Soul), 19 (all M7), 20 (all m7), 21 (all M9)

techno.name: Berlin techno
techno.why: Mostly 130-140 (minimal 124-130); Phrygian for dark techno; stabs and pedals, not progressions.

melodictechno.name: Melodic techno
melodictechno.why: 120-125 BPM, minor keys only, chords change every 2 or 4 bars.

ukg.name: UK garage / 2-step
ukg.why: ~130-134 BPM with heavy swing (60%); m7/m9 in Am/Cm/Dm; stabs share the bass rhythm.

dnb.name: Liquid drum & bass
dnb.why: 174 BPM (liquid 165-175), extended chords, sub in the D#1-G#1 sweet spot.

trap.name: Trap / dark pop
trap.why: 140-160 BPM felt in half-time; natural/harmonic minor and Phrygian; sparse chords leave room for the 808.

ambient.name: Ambient / cinematic
ambient.why: Slow modal vamps, sus/maj7/add9 open voicings, pedal tones.

futuregarage.name: Future garage / chillwave
futuregarage.why: Future garage 130-140 with thinned 2-step drums and slow minor sus2/m7 pads; chillwave 80-110.

follow-bass.why: Garage stabs use the same MIDI rhythm as the bassline, with the notes shortened.

held.why: Hold each chord a bar or more; also how the 'Can You Feel It' organ is played.

offbeat.why: Short stabs on the 'and' of each beat, mirroring the offbeat hat.

single-stab.why: Acid runs with no chords or a single stab: one hit per bar.

syncopated.why: 16th stab that skips the main drum hits and favours offbeat 16ths (...x|..x.|.x..|..x.).

j6-up-16.why: J-6 styles 1-2 are up/down arps at various speeds; this is the 16th speed over the pad voicing.

j6-updown-8.why: J-6 styles 1-2 are up/down arps at various speeds; this is the 8th-note speed over the pad voicing.

mt-pluck.why: Plucked 16th arp cycling the chord tones (short decay, low sustain).

one-octave.why: Arp set to a 1-octave range holding one note: root and octave in 16ths.

p1-3-over-4.why: A note every 3 sixteenths walking up the chord, so it lands on a different 16th each beat. Accents fall where the cycle meets a beat (every 12 steps). On the S-1 a 3-step loop (SHIFT+pad 4 (LAST), VALUE = 3) gives the rhythm; enter all 64 steps to keep the moving chord tones.

p2-33334.why: Trance cross-rhythm x..x..x..x..x... cut short to realign with every bar. Last step 16 (no change needed).

p6-6-step.why: Techno polymeter: this part repeats every 6 steps against the 16-step kick. On the S-1: SHIFT+pad 4 (LAST) + VALUE = 6.

p8-loop-28.why: Eno-style unsynchronised loops: this part repeats every 7 beats (28 steps), the lead every 5, so they drift. S-1 last step = 28.

sw-updown.why: 16th arp, Up/Down mode over root, 3rd, 5th, octave.

808-1.why: 808 on the kick, sliding up an octave (half-time bar).

808-2.why: 808 glides to the b3 and back to the root.

ac-b1.why: Phuture 'Acid Tracks': 8 steps looped twice per bar. The octave reading of the 303 up/down flags is the researcher's; octaves are folded into C1-C3 here.

ac-b2.why: Josh Wink 'Higher State' idea: two notes (root and major 3rd), accents on steps 10 and 13. Exact note order is not in the source; this is a placeholder.

ac-b4.why: Straight 16ths on 1-2 pitches, slides into octave jumps, accents on offbeats.

ac-b5-13.why: AC-B4 cut to 13 steps so it drifts against the bar ('woozy'). On the S-1: SHIFT+pad 4 (LAST), VALUE = 13, and enter just the first 13 steps.

ac-b6-lanes.why: Accent and slide lanes of different lengths from the note lane (16/7/5), written out over 64 steps. The S-1 has one pattern length, so keep last step = 64 and use these 64 steps as-is.

am-b1.why: Drone / pedal on the tonic, one note tied across all four bars.

ch-b1.why: Repetitive, hooky, octave-jumping and syncopated, locked to the kick.

db-b1.why: Sub on every kick of the two-step (steps 1 and 11), long notes on the chord root.

db-b2.why: Reese: legato notes on the two-step kick that glide into each other.

db-b4.why: Rolling offbeat (x..x|..x.|..xx|.x..) weaving around the kick.

db-p7.why: One new bass note every three 8ths (A C E A F E in A minor) under one shared upper shape, so the bass alone changes the chord. 36-step cycle: S-1 last step = 36.

dh-b1.why: Offbeat 8th on the 'and' of each beat, ducked by the kick; long offbeat notes.

dh-b2.why: Root on the beat moved partly to offbeats, plus octave leaps.

dh-b3.why: Tresillo 3-3-2 on steps 1, 7, 13. Fits a normal 16-step S-1 pattern.

dh-b4.why: Kerri Chandler pedal: the bass holds the tonic while the chords move.

fg-b1.why: Long sine sub on the 2-step kick positions (steps 1 and 11).

lf-b1.why: Root on beat 1, mostly root and 5th. Apply 55-60% swing on the OP-XY.

lf-b2.why: Root with a ghost offbeat octave, then the 5th.

lf-b2-12.why: LF-B2 folded into a 3/4 bar that drifts against the 4/4 chords. On the S-1: SHIFT+pad 4 (LAST), VALUE = 12.

lf-b3.why: Walking line: chord tones, then a half-step into the next chord's root (jazz source).

mt-offbeat-ghost.why: Offbeat 8ths with a ghost 16th (vel 64) just before the next kick.

mt-tresillo-10.why: 16 slots with 10 filled on a tresillo backbone (x.xx|.xx.|xx.x|.xx.).

sw-b2.why: Root repeated in 16ths, following the chord root each bar.

sw-b3.why: 16th octave bass: the 1-octave arp on one note.

sw-b4.why: Darksynth gallop x.xx with octave pickups.

tb-1.why: Rolling 16ths with the first 16th of each beat left empty for the kick.

tb-1-phrygian.why: Rolling 16ths off the kick, 0 0 1 variant for the Phrygian b2.

tb-3.why: EBM: all 16 steps on, octave on the 3rd 16th of each beat; distort it.

tb-5.why: Near-continuous 16ths on 3 notes (0 7 0 3); add swing and velocity variation.

uk-b1.why: Skippy line following the 2-step kick, b7 pickup. Swing ~60% on the OP-XY.

uk-b2.why: Long sub notes (x---|--x-|--x-|----) for a slow-attack 'wub'.

acid-303-lead.why: Acid has no separate lead in the research: a second 303-style line (16ths, octave jumps with slides) up in the lead register.

chop.why: Pitched vocal-chop style hits on chord tones, placed around the 2-step kick.

dnb-motif.why: No DnB lead in the research: long chord-tone motif (the general rule) that sits over the half-time feel.

dotted-8th.why: Notes every 3 sixteenths, cut short to realign each bar. Add a dotted-8th delay (45000/BPM ms) for the synthwave 'waterfall'.

house-motif.why: No house-specific lead in the research: a chord-tone motif with repetition (the general rule), placed on offbeats like the stabs.

lf-motif.why: Sparse 4-note motif stepping down from the tonic (C-B-A-G in C), repeated with rhythmic variation and rests.

mt-motif.why: Chord-tone motif A-C-E-D (in A minor), sequenced up a 4th (D-F-A-G), then back.

p6-5-step.why: Hypnotic polymetric lead: a 3-note figure repeating every 5 steps. S-1 last step = 5.

p8-loop-20.why: Unsynchronised loop: repeats every 5 beats (20 steps) while the arp repeats every 7. S-1 last step = 20.

sw-motif.why: Motif from chord tones, repeated and transposed, doubled an octave up the second time round. Detuned saw with moderate portamento.

trap-bells.why: Bell lead in a high octave: a call in the first half of each bar, a response in the gap.
